label: paragraph_title
text: IN SHEEP'S CLOTHING.

label: text
text: When the late Keir Hardie was was on his way to India about eighteen years ago he was interviewed in Penang by the present writer, and expressed views as sane and as reasonable as could be expected from the then leader of the Labour Party. When he reached India he got into the wrong hands, was shown "India" from "the extremists' point of view, was taken to places where everything had obviously been carefully stage managed by the worst type of, seditionist. He left India full to the brim of tales and "examples" of British tyranny and oppression, his mind

label: text
text:
those who acted as his guides, his opinions warped completely against the British Raj. There was as much difference between Keir Hardie in Penang and the Keir Hardie at Home subsequently as there is between chalk and cheese. The extremists had one their vile and shameless work! Mr. John Smith, late Professor of Education in the Hongkong University, seems to have followed in the footsteps of Keir Hardie, only that he went to Canton instead of India. He went as a self-accredited mediator to learn all there was of the Canton view of the boycott, to secure honourable terms of settlement, and to show the world what a very clever man Mr. John Smith was, and what bunglers were those other negotiators acting on behalf of Hongkong. He went; he saw; and he was conquered by the Bolshevik extremists in and advisers of Canton. There is no possible resemblance between Professor John Smith, of the Hongkong University, and Mr. John Smith, late of the Hongkong University, who is now recuperating under the protection of the good old Union. Jack in Britain.
In the Canton Gazette is published in the biggest and most glaring type it can commandeer the full account of Mr. John Smith's views on the boycott. To those Chinese who can read English but who may not ponder to think of all that account implies, Mr. John Smith may be lauded irrespective of the fact that he has

label: text
text: turned round on the hand that fed him in Hongkong and is still feeding him in Britain. A greater travesty of the truth could not emanate from M. Borodin or M. Karakhan, the Bolshevist emissaries in China, than this vituperative outburst from the pen of Mr. John Smith. It is unthinkable that it will appeal in the slightest degree to any right-thinking Chinese, either in Canton or Hongkong, or to the most authoritative circles in London or elsewhere. All that Mr. Smith has done is to strike a dustardly blow at his own fellow British subjects, heedless of the possible consequence of it rebounding, boomerang-like, on his own perverted head.

label: text
text: As a writer of "fiction" Mr. Smith should have a future before him. As a comrade of Trebitsch Lincoln, the renegade British M.P., he should gain at least notoriety. As an honest British subject "his presence in London or in any British Colony is an insult" to the Union Jack. Nobody who troubles to read his diatribes against the British, and against Hongkong in particular, is likely to be in the slightest degree affected. Of converts to the cause of Canton, which he has so suddenly espoused, he will make none. He will stand convicted of sedition and treason to his native land, and wherever he may go in future the hand of every sane, reasonable, and decent Briton will be turned against him. The derisive finger of scorn is all that is likely to be his reward for his despicable attempt to trample Hongkong in the dust of Canton.

label: paragraph_title
text: ROYAL BIRTHDAY.

label: paragraph_title
text: EMPEROR YOSHIHITO OF JAPAN.

label: text
text: OBSERVANCE LATER:

label: text
text: To-morrow is the birthday of the Emperor of Japan.

label: text
text: Celebrations are held later in the year on account of the heat (in Japan) at this time of the year.

label: text
text: The present Mikado, Yoshihito, was born at Tokyo in 1879. He succeeded his father on July 30, 1912, and was married on May 10, 1900.

label: text
text: On November 25, 1921, owing to the continued ill-health of the Emperor, the present Crown's prince (Hirohito) was constituted legent.

label: text
text: The Japanese claim that their empire was founded by the first Emperor, Jimmu Tenno, in B.C. 660, and that the dynasty founded by him still reigns.

label: text
text: By the Imperial House Law of 1889, the succession to the throne has been definitely fixed upon the male descendants.

label: text
text: The Hongkong Hockey Club will hold their annual meeting at 5.30 p.m. on Monday next in the lecture room, /Volunteer Headquarters.

label: text
text: CEREMONY AT ST. JOHN'S CATHEDRAL

label: text
text: WHEELER—FOWLER.

label: text
text: St. John's Cathedral was the scene of a pretty wedding on Saturday afternoon, the parties being Edith Mary Fowler, eldest daughter of Mr. and Mrs. G. Fowler, of the China Sugar Refinery, East Point; and Henry G. K. Wheeler, eldest son of Mr. and Mrs. G. Wheeler of Southampton, England.

label: text
text: The Rev. H. Copley Moyle conducted the service.

label: text
text: The bride, who entered the church on the arm of her father, by whom she was given away, wore an "very satin" dress, trimmed with silver face and orange blossoms with train and veil of white silk net and orange blossom wreath. She carried the bouquet of white roses and made denhair fern.

label: text
text: The Misses Annie Fowler (sister of the bride) and Babs Bliss, bridesmaids, wore, peach coloured crepe-de-chine dresses with gold shoes and hat to match, and carried bouquets of peach blooms and maidenhair.

label: text
text: The Misses Edna Stephens and Florrie Fowler (sister of the bride), train bearers, wore white satin and georgette petal frocks, satin slippers and silver tissue coronets, their bouquets being of white roses and maidenhair.

label: text
text: The bride's mother was attired in old rose georgette.

label: text
text: Mr. G. Flynn, of the Chinese Customs' Lappa, acted as best man, and Mr. M. J. Davidson, of the Chinese Customs, Kowloon, was groomsman.

label: text
text: No. 1 Great George Street, East point, the happy couple leaving for their honeymoon at Repulse Bay, preparatory to departure for Amoy and Foochow.

label: text
text: "The going away dress was of old rose crepe-de-chine trimmed with fawn, fawn shoes and stockings and hat to match. The bridegroom's present to the bride was a silver dressing set. The bride's present to bridegroom consisted of gold studs and sleeve links and the bridegroom's to the bride's attendants, gold and ruby brooches."

label: paragraph_title
text: QUEEN WILHELMINA'S BIRTHDAY.

label: text
text: CONSUL "AT HOME."

label: text
text: Residents of Holland celebrate the birthday of their Queen Wilhelmina to-morrow.

label: text
text: Queen Wilhelmina Helena Pauline Maria was born on August 31, 1880, the daughter of King Willem III and his second wife, Princess Emma of Waldeck.

label: text
text: On the death of her father she succeeded to the Dutch throne on November 23, 1890. Coming of age, she was crowned on September 6, in 1898.

label: text
text: In 1901 she was married to Prince Henry of Mecklenburg-Schwerin.

label: text
text: A daughter, Princess Juliana was born in 1909.

label: text
text: The present royal family of the Netherlands is known as the House of Orange.

label: text
text: There are quite a number of Dutch institutions in Hongkong. The J.C.J.L. is a very important shipping office, there are a few business hongs, the Netherlands Harbour Works Co. (North Point and Macao), a social club, and a tennis club.

label: text
text: To-morrow the local Consult General will be at home at the Chancery, between 11 and noon.
